A 47-year-old male comes to the emergency department with complaints of fatigue and a 7-pound
weight loss over the past month. His wife has noticed yellowing of his eyes, and he reports mild nausea
without vomiting, abdominal pain, or stool changes. His medical history includes an episode of acute

pancreatitis 10 years ago, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and obesity. He drinks two glasses of wine
daily and has a 30-pack-year smoking history. Vital signs show temperature 99.0°F (37°C), blood
pressure 141/67 mmHg, pulse 64/min, and respirations 13/min. Physical examination reveals icteric
sclera and a soft, non-tender abdomen with normal bowel sounds. Laboratory results show: - ALT: 67
U/L - AST: 54 U/L - Alkaline phosphatase: 771 U/L - Total bilirubin: 12.1 g/dL - Direct bilirubin: 9.4 g/dL
What finding would most likely be observed on abdominal imaging? Answer Choices: (A) Surface
nodularity of the liver (B) Acute choledocholithiasis (C) Dilated intrahepatic bile ducts (D) Hepatic
hemangioma (E) Distended gallbladder (F) Pancreatic pseudocyst (G) Gallbladder wall thickening (H)
Pancreatic mass with bile duct compression (I) Chronic pancreatitis with calcifications (J) Hepatic
metastases
 A. Hepatic hemangioma
B. Hepatic metastases
C. Surface nodularity of the liver
D. Gallbladder wall thickening
E. Acute choledocholithiasis
F. Chronic pancreatitis with calcifications
G. Dilated intrahepatic bile ducts
H. Distended gallbladder
I. Pancreatic pseudocyst
J. Pancreatic mass with bile duct compression
